source.title: Push the Student to Learn Right: Progressive Gradient Correcting by Meta-learner on Corrupted Labels
source.authors: Jun Shu; Qi Xie; Li-Xuan Yi; Qian Zhao; Sanping Zhou; Zong-Ben Xu; De-Yu Meng

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though the appendix contains OCR/formatting errors and some figure data are not numerically recoverable.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training and test accuracy behavior under corrupted-label training, using a different setting and method from the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that its baseline overfits noisy labels while MW-Net and L2RW are less prone to overfitting (Appendix G, Fig. 7). These are results about corrupted-label training, not the specific conditions or measurements named by V1–V8. The paper also discusses cited prior work; those results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates sample weighting for class imbalance and partially corrupted labels. It does not test any of V1–V8. In particular, noisy-label overfitting does not establish V1's paired comparison of near-perfect random-label fitting and natural-label generalization. The study cites original generalization research as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that MW-Net learns explicit sample-weighting functions from a small unbiased meta-dataset and improves robustness under class imbalance, corrupted labels, and real-world data bias. Appendix G additionally describes reduced noisy-label overfitting and faster convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains with a learned sample-weighting meta-network using clean meta-data; the mapped versions concern generalization conditions or measurements on natural-label tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and uniform-noise rate vary across the Appendix G figure panels; the text does not quantify their effects there.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix G describes declining baseline test accuracy after learning-rate decay and more stable test accuracy with MW-Net and L2RW under partially corrupted labels. These are robustness and mitigation results, not the random-label capacity comparison in V1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Meta-learned sample weighting can reduce overfitting to partially corrupted training labels and preserve clean-test accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: 33rd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2019), Vancouver, Canada
record.problems: The relevant accuracy curves are figure-only and do not provide recoverable numerical values in the supplied text; the paper's main experiments concern biased training data rather than the mapped natural-label settings.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels, chance held-out accuracy under random labels, and natural-label generalization with the same architecture and recipe.
Classifier width sweeps beyond zero training error. Appendix E varies the weighting network's architecture, not classifier width past interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples, followed by retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures do not instantiate those versions; this does not negate the authors' explicit qualitative overfitting findings. Figure 7 uses mini-batch noisy-training accuracy and clean-test accuracy. No omitted result in the supplied text warrants a verdict on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural labels for the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons on images.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.
Removal of memorized examples and the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: BaseModel
rows.operation_detail: Trained on noisy labels; training and test accuracy tracked over epochs.
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy curves; authors state the model overfits noisy labels and test accuracy degrades after the first learning-rate decay.
rows.note: The text describes the trend but provides no recoverable numerical values.
rows.check: The classifier is WRN-28-10. Appendix G explicitly reports noisy-label overfitting, but this does not measure any claim version. Mini-batch training accuracy on partially corrupted labels cannot establish V1.

rows.subject: Ours

rows.measure: Training and test accuracy curves; authors say it is less prone to overfitting and retains similar test accuracy until termination.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative comparison but no recoverable numerical values.
rows.check: This is WRN-28-10 trained using MW-Net, a method-performance result outside V1–V8. Figure 7(a) follows MW-Net beyond 40 epochs; the authors report peak performance around 40 epochs.
